text.en: Ainu lacks genitive case marking for expressing possession ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ainu-lacks-genitive-case⟧. The possessive constructions that exist are typologically typical and are fully accounted for by the cross-linguistic framework of nominal argument structure, valence, and appositive possession ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ainu-possession-typologically-typical⟧. Bugaeva proposes that Ainu may be interpreted as a remnant of an earlier, larger group of North Asian Circum-Pacific languages with appositive possession, the others having been absorbed by expansions of Tungusic, Japonic, Korean, Sinitic, and Austronesian ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ainu-remnant-north-asian-appositive⟧. Possessive expressions corresponding to Japanese 'Noun1 no Noun2' take three types of constructions: (1) N1 *kor* N2, (2) N1 N2 with an affiliative form, and (3) juxtaposition of two concept-form nouns ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--three-possessive-construction-types⟧. In constructions (1) and (2), Noun1 can be replaced by a transitive-subject personal prefix such as *ku=*, whereas in construction (3) this substitution is not possible ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--constructions-1-2-allow-prefix-not-3⟧. The nominal possessive expression takes the form of the possessor noun followed by the possessive, or affiliative, form of the possessed noun, and the genitive precedes the head noun ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--possessor-precedes-possessed-affiliative⟧⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--genitive-precedes-head-noun⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語には所有を表す属格格標示が存在しない⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ainu-lacks-genitive-case⟧。存在する所有構文は極めて典型的であり、名詞の項構造・結合価と同格所有に関する通言語的枠組みによって十全に説明される⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ainu-possession-typologically-typical⟧。Bugaevaは、アイヌ語を、同格所有を有していた北アジア環太平洋諸言語のかつて存在したより大きな集団の残存として解釈できると提案しており、他の言語群はツングース系、日琉系、朝鮮系、中国系、オーストロネシア系の拡大に吸収されたとする⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ainu-remnant-north-asian-appositive⟧。日本語で「名詞₁の名詞₂」と訳されるアイヌ語の所有表現には、(1) 名詞₁ *kor* 名詞₂、(2) 名詞₁に所属形の名詞₂が後続する形、(3) 2つの概念形名詞の並置という3通りの構文がある⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--three-possessive-construction-types⟧。構文(1)と(2)では名詞₁を*ku=*などの他動詞主語人称接辞に置き換えることができるが、構文(3)ではこの置き換えができない⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--constructions-1-2-allow-prefix-not-3⟧。名詞の所有表現は所有者名詞に被所有名詞の所属形が後続する形をとり、属格名詞は主要部名詞に先行する⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--possessor-precedes-possessed-affiliative⟧⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--genitive-precedes-head-noun⟧。

text.en: The third-person possessor prefix is zero, so a possessed noun form standing alone by default means 'his/her/its …' ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--third-person-possessor-prefix-zero⟧. A noun in its affiliative person form, such as *siki*, indexes the possessor internally and can stand alone to express a possessed meaning, making an independent possessor noun phrase grammatically optional ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--affiliative-form-possessor-optional-np⟧.
text.ja: 三人称所有者接頭辞はゼロであるため、所有接尾辞形の名詞が単独で立つ場合のデフォルトの解釈は「彼／彼女／それの…」となる⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--third-person-possessor-prefix-zero⟧。*siki*のような名詞の人称形は人称接辞によって名詞内部に所有者の人称が表示されているため単独で完結した所属の意味を表すことができ、対応する所有者名詞句は文法的に必須ではない⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--affiliative-form-possessor-optional-np⟧。

text.en: The affiliative form of a noun indexes the person and number of the possessor via the A-series, that is transitive-subject, cross-reference prefixes such as *ku=*, *ci=*, *e=*, *eci=*, and *a=* ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--affiliative-indexes-possessor-via-a-series⟧. The nominal possessive expression takes the form of the possessor noun followed by the affiliative form of the possessed noun ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--possessor-precedes-possessed-affiliative⟧. Expressions consisting of a pronoun or noun plus a personal form of a noun do not strictly form a single tight noun phrase corresponding to Japanese 'A no B'; rather, the bond between A and B is weak ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--weak-bond-pronoun-personal-form⟧, and other syntactic elements such as particles can intervene between the possessor noun phrase and the possessed noun ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--intervening-elements-possessor-possessum⟧. Because using genitive pronouns is mechanically simpler than forming concrete forms for each noun, the genitive construction expanded and led to double-marking expressions such as *akor amachihi* 'my wife' ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--double-marking-diachronic-expansion⟧. By analogy from *kor mat* = *kor machihi*, forms such as *akor machihi* or *ekor machihi* have begun to appear even among Ainu speakers, though traditional elders strictly avoid this ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--akor-machihi-analogical-error⟧.
text.ja: 名詞の所属形には、*ku=*・*ci=*・*e=*・*eci=*・*a=*などのA（他動詞主語）系列の相互参照接頭辞によって所有者の人称・数が標示される⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--affiliative-indexes-possessor-via-a-series⟧。名詞の所有表現は所有者名詞に被所有名詞の所属形が後続する形をとる⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--possessor-precedes-possessed-affiliative⟧。代名詞または名詞と名詞の人称形からなる表現は、厳密には日本語の「AのB」というひとまとまりの句をなしているわけではなく、AとBの結びつきは弱い⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--weak-bond-pronoun-personal-form⟧。また、所有者名詞句と被所有名詞の間に助詞などの要素が介在して分断されることがごく普通に起きる⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--intervening-elements-possessor-possessum⟧。領格代名詞を用いる表現は機械的で労力が少なくて済むため歓迎されて領域を拡大し、最終的には*akor amachihi*「私の妻」のような二重標示表現を生むに至った⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--double-marking-diachronic-expansion⟧。*kor mat* = *kor machihi*からの類推により、*akor machihi*や*ekor machihi*のような表現がアイヌ自身の間でも用いられそうになっているが、古格を守る古老の言語では絶対に生じない⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--akor-machihi-analogical-error⟧。

text.en: Inalienable and alienable possessive constructions can combine into larger syntactic structures ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--inalienable-alienable-combine-nested⟧.
text.ja: 譲渡不能所有構文と譲渡可能所有構文は組み合わさってより大きな統語構造を形成することができる⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--inalienable-alienable-combine-nested⟧。

text.en: Ainu has an appositive classifier system that uses verbs ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ainu-verbal-appositive-classifier-system⟧. In the alienable possessive construction, the possessor is coded not as a dependent within a noun phrase but as an argument in a finite clause, and the appositive word is a verb ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--alienable-possessor-as-verbal-argument⟧. Alienable nouns use a relative construction with *kor* 'have', in which the possessor is marked as the subject of *kor* and the possessed noun is the gapped object ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-relative-clause-alienable-possession⟧. The person markers used in this construction are unambiguously verbal person markers ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--alienable-person-markers-verbal⟧, and the appositive verb modifying the possessed noun is finite ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--appositive-verb-is-finite⟧. Refsing, analysing Shizunai Ainu, asserts that *kor* functions as an attributive postposition when placed directly between two nouns or between a pronominal affix and a noun ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-between-nouns-attributive-postposition⟧, and reports that most expressions of possession in Shizunai Ainu are constructed with *kor* ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--shizunai-most-possession-via-kor⟧; Satō similarly notes that *kor* is used as a marker expressing possession in Chitose Ainu ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-marker-of-possession-chitose⟧. Bugaeva, by contrast, analyses the possessor in the *kor* construction as an argument of a finite verb, not as a dependent in a noun phrase ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--alienable-possessor-as-verbal-argument⟧, a position that contrasts with Refsing's postpositional analysis ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-between-nouns-attributive-postposition⟧. Kindaichi and Chiri assert that *kor* can only be used to express possession when the possessor has personhood ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-genitive-only-with-personhood⟧, a restriction that differs in scope from Bugaeva's account of the construction ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-relative-clause-alienable-possession⟧. The genitive relation of personal pronouns can also be expressed by *kor* with an appropriate personal affix followed by the possessed noun ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-personal-affix-genitive-pronouns⟧. When the possessor is third person, *kor* lacks overt person marking and tends to form a single phonological unit with the following possessum head noun, preceded by a pause after the possessor noun phrase ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-third-person-zero-phonological-unit⟧. The predicate *kor* can optionally be marked for verbal plurality ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-optional-verbal-plurality⟧, perfectivity ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-optional-perfectivity⟧, or mirativity ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-optional-mirativity⟧, and can take adverbial modifiers ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-takes-adverbial-modifiers⟧. The *kor* construction with human nouns and human attributes is used with high frequency in Saru Ainu partly due to an extended affective function expressing affection ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-human-nouns-affective-frequency⟧. Ainu is described as having a one-classifier verbal appositive possessive system ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ainu-one-classifier-verbal-appositive⟧, with *kor* as the sole classifier ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--sole-classifier-is-verb⟧, though Bugaeva also characterises the verbal appositives as a small system of one or two verbs meaning 'own' or 'have' ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--verbal-appositives-one-or-two-verbs⟧. The several possessive classifiers of earlier Ainu have shrunk to just one in the modern variety ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--classifiers-shrunk-to-one-modern⟧. In oral literature, a number of transitive verbs other than *kor* functioned as possessive classifiers specifying the type of possessive relation in prenominal relative clauses ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--transitive-verbs-as-possessive-classifiers-oral-lit⟧: *un* 'attach to, belong' in expressions like *a-un cise* 'my house' ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--un-classificatory-possessive-verb⟧, *mut* 'wear (a sword)' in expressions like *a-mut emusi* 'my sword' ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--mut-classificatory-possessive-verb⟧, *an-te* (causative of *an* 'exist') in *e-an-te hoku* 'your husband' ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ante-classificatory-possessive-verb⟧, *hekote* 'be married to' with spouse and family terms ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--hekote-classificatory-possessive-verb⟧, and *mi* 'wear' in expressions like *a-mi kosonde* 'my kimono' ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--mi-classificatory-possessive-verb⟧. In older Ainu, larger appositive classifier systems added subdivisions of food by preparation type, clothing, instruments and objects by function, fire and fire-related things, houses, and various items by history of acquisition ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--older-ainu-larger-classifier-subdivisions⟧. A larger verbal classifier system is reconstructible for earlier Ainu, in which classifiers relate to the history and cultural status of possession ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--larger-classifier-system-reconstructible⟧, and Bugaeva proposes that when Ainu was still the daily language of a large speech community it had multiple alienable class constructions ⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--earlier-ainu-multiple-alienable-classes⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語には動詞を用いる同格分類詞体系が存在する⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ainu-verbal-appositive-classifier-system⟧。譲渡可能所有標示において、所有者は名詞句内の従属部としてではなく定形節の項としてコード化され、同格語は動詞である⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--alienable-possessor-as-verbal-argument⟧。譲渡可能名詞は*kor*「持つ」を用いた関係節構文を使用し、所有者が*kor*の主語として標示され、被所有名詞は*kor*の空所化された目的語となる⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-relative-clause-alienable-possession⟧。この構文で用いられる人称標識は明白に動詞の人称標識であり⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--alienable-person-markers-verbal⟧、被所有名詞を修飾する同格動詞は定形である⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--appositive-verb-is-finite⟧。Refsing は静内アイヌ語を分析し、*kor*が2つの名詞の間または人称接辞と名詞の間に直接置かれるとき連体助詞として機能すると主張し⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-between-nouns-attributive-postposition⟧、静内アイヌ語における所有表現の大半が*kor*を用いて構成されると報告する⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--shizunai-most-possession-via-kor⟧。Satō も同様に、千歳アイヌ語において*kor*が所有を表す形式として用いられると指摘する⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-marker-of-possession-chitose⟧。これに対しBugaevaは、*kor*構文における所有者を名詞句内の従属部としてではなく定形動詞の項として分析しており⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--alienable-possessor-as-verbal-argument⟧、この立場はRefsing の後置詞分析と対立する⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-between-nouns-attributive-postposition⟧。Kindaichi と Chiri は、*kor*が所有を表すために用いられるのは所有者が人格を有する場合に限られると主張しており⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-genitive-only-with-personhood⟧、この制約はBugaevaによる構文の記述とは適用範囲が異なる⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-relative-clause-alienable-possession⟧。人称代名詞の属格関係は、適切な人称接辞を伴う*kor*に被所有名詞が後続する形によっても表されうる⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-personal-affix-genitive-pronouns⟧。所有者が3人称の場合、*kor*は明示的な人称標示を欠き、所有者名詞句の後に休止を伴って後続の被所有主要部名詞と単一の音調単位を形成する傾向がある⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-third-person-zero-phonological-unit⟧。述語*kor*は任意で動詞の複数性標示⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-optional-verbal-plurality⟧、完了相標示⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-optional-perfectivity⟧、またはミラティビティ標示⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-optional-mirativity⟧を受けることができ、副詞的修飾語を伴うことも可能である⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-takes-adverbial-modifiers⟧。サル方言において、人間名詞や人間の属性を表す名詞とともに*kor*構文の頻度が高いのは、愛情を表す派生的な用法の存在が一因と報告されている⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--kor-human-nouns-affective-frequency⟧。アイヌ語は分類詞を1つだけ持つ動詞同格所有体系を有すると記述され⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ainu-one-classifier-verbal-appositive⟧、*kor*がその唯一の分類詞とされる⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--sole-classifier-is-verb⟧が、Bugaevaは動詞同格語を「所有する」または「持つ」を意味する1つまたは2つの動詞からなる小さな体系とも特徴づけている⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--verbal-appositives-one-or-two-verbs⟧。より古い段階のアイヌ語に存在した複数の所属類別詞は、現代の変種においてはただ1つにまで減少している⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--classifiers-shrunk-to-one-modern⟧。口承文芸において、*kor*以外のいくつかの他動詞が前置名詞修飾関係節において所有関係の種類を指定する所有分類詞として機能していた⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--transitive-verbs-as-possessive-classifiers-oral-lit⟧。具体的には、*a-un cise*「私の家」のような表現における*un*「〜につく、〜に属する」⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--un-classificatory-possessive-verb⟧、*a-mut emusi*「私の刀」のような表現における*mut*「（刀を）帯びる」⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--mut-classificatory-possessive-verb⟧、*e-an-te hoku*「あなたの夫」における*an-te*（*an*「存在する」の使役形）⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--ante-classificatory-possessive-verb⟧、配偶者や親族の語とともに用いられる*hekote*「〜と結婚している」⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--hekote-classificatory-possessive-verb⟧、および*a-mi kosonde*「私の着物」のような表現における*mi*「着る」⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--mi-classificatory-possessive-verb⟧がある。より古い時代のアイヌ語における大規模な同格的所有分類詞体系では、調理形態による食物の細分化、衣服、機能による道具や物品、火および火に関連する事物、家屋、獲得の経緯による様々な品目などが付け加わる⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--older-ainu-larger-classifier-subdivisions⟧。初期のアイヌ語には、分類詞が所有の歴史や文化的地位に関与する、より大規模な動詞的分類詞体系が再構可能であり⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--larger-classifier-system-reconstructible⟧、Bugaevaはアイヌ語が大規模な言語共同体の日常言語であった際には複数の譲渡可能名詞クラス構文を有していたと提案している⟦claim:nominal/adnominal-possession-double-marking--earlier-ainu-multiple-alienable-classes⟧。
